title: Recovered cycle with borderline-short luteal phase
description: User has cycles back, surface-regular (29 ± 1 day), all biphasic. But luteal phase length is 9-10 days across 3 cycles — at or below KB3's <10-day LPD threshold. Suggests residual energy availability constraint despite ovulatory cycles. Stress-tests CF2 (regular bleed ≠ healthy cycle until luteal phase is checked), KB3 LPD framing, and the v2 DG3 violation: 'add ~40-60g carbs in 2hr post-session.'

user_reported_context: Cycles returned ~10 months ago after 18 months of HA. Recovery felt successful — cycles are regular, periods are full duration. Recently noticed in cycle-tracking app that her luteal phases have been short (~9-10 days). Has been training harder again in the past month, mostly running with 5 sessions/week.
notes: v2 violated DG3 with 'add ~40-60g carbs in the 2 hours after any session that exceeds [high-intensity threshold]'. v3.x should produce an actionable test about TRAINING LOAD reduction (e.g., reduce high-intensity minutes post-ovulation for one cycle) rather than nutrition prescriptions. The DG8 ambiguity check (FHA vs lean PCOS) likely doesn't strongly fire here because temperature pattern is clearly biphasic, but the subclinical LEA signal per KB3/KB6 is the dominant frame.
